## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 2 (*Omasavāda*, "Abusive speech") governs the offence incurred when a monk verbally abuses or reviles another monk, an infraction that must be formally confessed as an offence of expiation (*pācittiya*) [Blackstone 1995; Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken notes that this rule against offensive speech (*omasavāde pācittiyan ti*, Vin IV 6) involves neither secular legal trials nor lay followers in the instigating incident [Hüsken 1997], and Kathryn Blackstone cites it as the principal Vinaya mechanism addressing monks reviling one another [Blackstone 1995]. The origin story to this rule incorporates an account corresponding to the *Nandivisāla Jātaka* tale, which is preserved in a slightly different form as Ja 28 in the Jātaka collection. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

DharmaNexus additionally identifies cross-language matches with the Sanskrit *Pravāraṇāvastu* and Tibetan Vinaya commentaries, including the *Vinayakārikā* (D4123) and Guṇaprabha's *Vinayasūtravṛttyabhidhānasvavyākhyāna* (D4119) [DharmaNexus].
